'''Mawayana''' (Mahuayana), also known as '''Mapidian''' (Maopidyán), is a moribund [[Arawakan language]] of northern South America. It used to be spoken by {{ill|Mawayana people|nl|Mawayana (volk)|lt=Mawayana}} people living in ethnic [[Wai-wai people|Wai-wai]] and [[Tiriyó people|Tiriyó]] villages in [[Brazil]], [[Guyana]] and [[Suriname]].<ref name="Meira-2019"/>{{sfn|Mans|Carlin|2015|p=98}} As of 2015, the last two speakers of the language are living in [[Kwamalasamutu]].{{sfn|Carlin|2006|p=317}}{{sfn|Mans|Carlin|2015|p=98}}

== History ==
In the 1840s, the Mawayana were in contact with the Taruma, but both groups have amalgamated with the [[Wai-wai people]], and those who joined have lost both their languages. Only two elderly women, who were part of a group of Mawayana who accompanied American missionaries to convert the [[Tiriyó people]], and subsequently moved in with them,<ref>{{Cite book |last=Carlin |first=Eithne |title=A grammar of Trio: a Cariban language of Suriname |date=2004 |publisher=Lang |isbn=978-0-8204-7358-1 |series=Duisburger Arbeiten zur Sprach- und Kulturwissenschaft |location=Frankfurt am Main}}</ref> still spoke the language in 2015, and their children did not speak Mawayana.<ref name=":0" /> A few rememberers exist who do not use it on a daily basis.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Hornborg |first=Alf |title=Ethnicity in ancient Amazonia: reconstructing past identities from archaeology, linguistics, and ethnohistory |last2=Hill |first2=Jonathan David |date=2011 |publisher=University Press of Colorado |isbn=978-1-60732-094-4 |location=Boulder, CO}}</ref>

== Classification ==
{{harvcoltxt|Aikhenvald|1999}} lists Mawayana (and possibly Mawakwa as a dialect) together with [[Wapishana language|Wapishana]] under a Rio Branco (North-Arawak) branch of the Arawakan family. {{harvcoltxt|Carlin|2006|p= 314}} notes that Mawayana "is closely related to Wapishana" and according to {{harvcoltxt|Ramirez|2001|p= 530}} they share at least 47% of their lexicon.

== Phonology ==
Mawayana has, among its consonants, two [[implosive consonant|implosives]], {{IPA|/ɓ/}} and {{IPA|/ɗ/}}, and what has been described as a "retroflex fricativised rhotic", represented with {{angbr|rž}}, that it shares with [[Wapishana language|Wapishana]]. The vowel systems contains four vowels ({{IPA|/i-e, a, ɨ, u-o/}}), each of which has a nasalised counterpart.<ref>{{harvcoltxt|Carlin|2006|p= 320}}</ref>

== Morphosyntax ==
Mawayana has a polysynthetic morphology, mainly head-marking and with suffixes, although there are pronominal prefixes. The verbal arguments are indexed on the verb through subject suffixes on intransitive verbs, while agent prefixes and object suffixes on transitive verbs.{{sfn|Carlin|2006}}{{rp|319}}

=== Verb roots ===
Verbal roots in Mawayana may be composed of at least one consonant ({{Lang|mzx|m-}} 'say', {{Lang|mzx|ch-}} 'do'), and the root must end in a consonant.<ref name=":0">{{Cite thesis |date=2014-08-29 |title=Verbal Morphology in Mawayana |url=https://studenttheses.universiteitleiden.nl/handle/1887/28661 |language=en |archive-url=http://web.archive.org/web/20240626151321/https://studenttheses.universiteitleiden.nl/handle/1887/28661 |archive-date=2024-06-26}}</ref>
